title: How Long Does Cooked Rice Last in the Fridge?

seo.title: How Long Cooked Rice Lasts in the Fridge
seo.meta_description: USDA leftover guidance allows 3–4 days, but rapid cooling is critical for rice because of Bacillus cereus. Learn how to store and reheat it safely.
seo.search_intent: Store cooked rice safely in a U.S. household context.

excerpt: USDA's general leftovers guidance is 3–4 days in the refrigerator, but cooked rice must be cooled promptly because Bacillus cereus spores can survive cooking and grow if rice sits warm.
content_html:
Cooked rice can be refrigerated, but cooling it promptly matters as much as the number of days. Rice can contain spores of Bacillus cereus that survive cooking and may grow if cooked rice remains warm for too long.

In the United States, USDA's general leftovers guidance is 3–4 days at 40°F / 4°C or below. A more conservative rice-specific approach used by the U.K. Food Standards Agency is to cool rice rapidly and use it within 24 hours. Whichever time limit you follow, long periods at room temperature are the bigger problem.

Safe rice routine

StepWhat to do
After cookingSet aside leftovers promptly
CoolingUse shallow containers; refrigerate within 2 hours
RefrigeratorUSDA general leftovers: 3–4 days
ReheatingHeat evenly to 165°F / 74°C

Why rice is associated with Bacillus cereus

B. cereus produces heat-resistant spores. Normal cooking destroys many active bacteria but can leave spores behind. If cooked rice sits warm, those spores can germinate and bacteria may multiply; some strains can produce heat-stable toxins.

Cool it quickly

A large pot of rice can stay warm in the center for a long time. Divide leftovers into shallow containers rather than leaving the entire pot on the counter. Refrigerate within 2 hours, or within 1 hour when the surrounding temperature is above 90°F / 32°C.

Why different countries give different storage times

USDA groups rice with general cooked leftovers at 3–4 days under proper refrigeration. The U.K. FSA uses a stricter rice-specific recommendation of 24 hours. Both emphasize rapid cooling because refrigeration cannot undo hours spent warm.

Can you eat rice cold?

Yes, if it was cooked, cooled and refrigerated properly. Cold rice itself is not the problem; poor time-temperature control is.

Reheating

Reheat leftovers to 165°F / 74°C. In a microwave, stir the rice and allow standing time so the center reaches temperature. Reheating cannot reliably fix rice that sat out overnight.

Takeout rice

With homemade rice, you know when it was cooked. Takeout adds uncertainty about holding and transport time. Refrigerate leftovers promptly after the meal rather than leaving the container out for the evening.

Freezing

Rice freezes well. If you will not use it soon, cool it promptly and freeze in meal-sized portions. Reheat thoroughly when serving.

Smell is not a safety test

Rice associated with B. cereus toxin can look and smell normal. Storage history is more informative than a sniff test.

Bottom line

For U.S. households, properly cooled rice fits USDA's 3–4 day leftover window, but it should be refrigerated within 2 hours and kept at 40°F/4°C or below. A 24-hour limit is a more conservative option. Never rely on reheating to rescue rice that sat warm for hours.

Sources

U.S. storage times come from FoodSafety.gov/USDA. Rice-specific Bacillus cereus guidance is also published by the Food Standards Agency.

faq.question: How many days can cooked rice stay in the fridge?
faq.answer: USDA general leftover guidance is 3–4 days at 40°F/4°C or below. The U.K. FSA uses a more conservative 24-hour rice-specific limit.

faq.question: Why is rice a food-safety concern?
faq.answer: Bacillus cereus spores can survive cooking and grow if rice remains warm for too long.

faq.question: Can reheating make rice safe after it sat out overnight?
faq.answer: No. Some toxins can be heat-stable, so reheating is not a reliable rescue step.
